title: Episode Six Adds Issuance and Redemption Checks for Tokenized Deposits
description: Verified Backing checks funds recorded on the issuer's ledger and outstanding issuance status, while banks retain responsibility for reserve assurance and regulatory obligations.
why_it_matters: Checking redemption requests before releasing money addresses an operational risk in tokenized banking, but ledger controls alone cannot establish actual reserve sufficiency.
keyTakeaways: Recorded backing checks do not replace reserve assurance.
body:
Episode Six announced Verified Backing on October 15 as part of its E6 Token Control Ledger. The feature covers supported bank-issued tokenized deposits and stablecoins. Before issuance, it checks the backing recorded in the ledger. At redemption, it checks that the token is genuine and remains outstanding before funds are released.

The company says the capability runs on the bank's side and is available to its customers in markets where it operates. Availability and functionality depend on the implementation and market.

The control does not hold, safeguard or attest to reserves. Issuers remain responsible for reserve, attestation, audit and regulatory obligations.

facts.claim: The control operates within the bank's ledger infrastructure.
Tokens must remain outstanding when presented for redemption.
The feature does not attest to an issuer's reserves.
